sense: a car engine, in children’s talk

evidence: Lucr. 6.581 (Lewis & Short s.v. fremō): of wind roaring in caves
terms.comment: No ancient form of the sound is known. The classical verb for a low roar (Lewis & Short: “to make a low roaring”), of wind, sea and beasts, applied by us to the engine.

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.116 (Lewis & Short s.v. fremitus): of the murmuring sea

phrases.english: Do you hear the car roaring?

sources: Lewis & Short: fremo · Lewis & Short: fremitus
No ancient form of the sound is known; the uses are ours, on the classical verb.
